findings.text: The import arm exists in the manifest only as 'same ids' prose: line 30 records counts (base 4 failed / 156 passed, head 4 failed / 156 passed) and names no failing id and no revision, while the two JSON objects the record does carry (baseline_suite/after_suite at manifest.md:24-25) name tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py and tests/test_every_shared_home_lock_holds_across_nodes.py, not the 25-file import arm. The done_when asks both arm results to be recorded as inline JSON carrying full 40-character revisions, so the shape is unmet in the record promotion reads; the substance is verifiable and I verified it, comparing import-arm-base.log and import-arm-head.log (25 test files each, identical four FAILED ids, both EXIT=1).

The done_when's 'ruff check and ruff format --check report nothing new on the changed paths' clause is answered by a claim in evidence_inputs with no command and no log path, so the lint result is asserted rather than recorded and cannot be re-run from the record.

notes: Scores are per dimension and independent. Durability: the diff adds no assertion, so the guard is the pre-existing case at tests/test_crew_record_liveness.py:181 (test_no_module_decides_record_liveness_with_a_bare_pid) whose assertion is 'assert offenders == {}' over an AST scan of LIVENESS_MODULES; reinstating the regression puts the record['pid'] shape back in recovery_liveness.py, which is one of the scanned modules, and the base log records exactly that id failing with 'assert {\'recovery_li...cord\': True}]} == {}' at 42fe90d0 with EXIT=1, so the assertion is independent of any value the test supplied and reddens on the exact code change it guards. The scanner carries its own positive control at tests/test_crew_record_liveness.py:193 ensuring the scan is not blind. It is pre-existing rather than added by this run, so it is not evidence the run wrote but it is a real guard over the landed line. Reuse: the change routes the stopped arm through runs.record_process_alive... see the record_process_alive owner at reckon/crew/process_liveness.py:453, which already owns the start-tick comparison and the placed-run and session-walk rules, and it matches the idiom the same module already uses at reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:312 (_worker_record_liveness hands in its own probe) and at :1777, so no capability is forked. Fit: one expression swapped, no new names, two conventional commit subjects with bodies. Added failures: baseline_suite and after_suite both record completed true, exit_status 0, failure_count 0 with empty failure_ids, so the delta is zero added failures, derived from those two gate logs rather than from the worker's account.
